notes: v5/v6 50-task: task_352 / 396 / 418 timed out 100% of the time at 900-1200s. Higher budget alone doesn't recover but partial credit becomes possible when the agent picks the streaming path.
prompt_hints: Heavy task detected (extreme tier or large context). Avoid loading entire files into memory.
Use SQL aggregations / streaming tools / dataframe_head with small max_rows. Do NOT call read_csv / read_json on huge files.

notes: task_249 (166MB) had aggregate question; full read_json times out before parsing finishes. Streaming aggregate computes the answer in seconds.
prompt_hints: Large JSON file (>=50MB) present. Do NOT call read_json — the response is capped and you will miss data.
Call streaming_json_keys first to discover the schema, then use streaming_json_count / streaming_json_aggregate for the answer.

notes: task_330 trace shows full-table reads exhaust the model context. Aggregate-first pattern keeps the prompt small.
prompt_hints: Large SQLite DB (>=100MB) present. Use SQL aggregations (SUM / AVG / COUNT / GROUP BY) and project only the columns you need.
Large CSV (>=50MB) present. Prefer dataframe_head with explicit small max_rows (10-50) over read_csv.
Use dataframe_describe to get the schema + value distributions before deciding how to filter / aggregate.
Aggregate question detected (avg / sum / count / min / max). Compute the value via TWO independent paths (e.g. SQL AND pandas).
If the two paths disagree, investigate before answering — value-mismatch with correct shape is the most common 0-score failure.
Plural question (list / which / who / all). Apply DISTINCT, count expected matches, and verify each row corresponds to a unique entity.

evidence: task_19 (zip5 vs zip9 mismatch — Illinois lookup never matched)

prompt_hints: Zip-code joins (chronic loop): when matching a member zip to a reference zip table, the two sides may use different formats (5-digit vs 9-digit ZIP+4). Cast both to the SAME width before comparison: try LEFT(zip, 5), CAST(zip AS TEXT), or strip non-digits. Source data style is BIRD-typical: ZIP+4 in one table, ZIP-5 in another.

evidence: task_80 (lap time string compare — '0:01:54' never matched)

prompt_hints: Time/duration string compare: when the question's filter value looks like '0:01:54' (H:MM:SS), the source column may store '1:54.000' (M:SS.ms) or seconds-only. Cast/format both sides before comparison; do not rely on string equality. If filter yields 0 rows AND the column min/max overlap the requested range, commit empty with confirm:true.
Singular question — the answer is a single value (1x1 table). Do NOT widen with bookkeeping columns or extra rows.
